answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each identity to a costly, non-transferable work history: a new agent must complete verifiable useful tasks and lock a stake before it earns full trust, like a pearl forming slowly layer by layer rather than appearing instantly. A haven that lets anyone in for free invites thousands of clones, but when every lotus-like fresh identity must pay time, compute, and stake that is slashed for cheating, an attacker must fund each fake separately, so Sybil scale becomes expensive, slow, and unprofitable.
